newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euris seen cutting Moulinex stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Euris seen cutting Moulinex stake - paper.

text.p: French holding company Euris, the main shareholder in Moulinex, would lower its stake in the appliance maker to seven percent from an indirect 33 percent under a planned restructuring of the group's capital, French daily Les Echos said on Wednesday.
Moulinex is set to reshuffle its shareholder structure, a typically French cascade of holding companies, before the end of the year.

The main changes would entail the absorption by Moulinex of the Financiere Moulinex and Finap holdings. Euris owns 33 percent of Financiere Moulinex, that in turn controls 100 percent of Finap. Finap owns 20.47 percent of Moulinex.
According to Les Echos, Finamex, the holding company regrouping the interests of the family of Moulinex founder Jean Mantelet, would end up with a seven percent stake.
The 5.5 percent direct interest held by international financier George Soros, would remain unchanged, it said.
Moulinex, which sparked an outcry last year when it announced a drastic restructuring plan returned to profit this year.
It reported a net attributable profit of 29 million francs for the year to March 31, 1997 against a loss of 702 million francs in the previous year.
Earlier this year it set a 525 million francs capital increase that was fully subscribed and has just launched a 300 million French francs bonds issue.
